property_summary: After any Deposit call by any actor sending a nonzero amount, the reference contract always increases that actor's balances entry by exactly the sent amount (balances[actor]_after == balances[actor]_before + amount); the mutant that subtracts msg.value from balances breaks this rule for some inputs.

For any address actor and any payable amount, calling Deposit() with that amount never decreases the contract's balances[actor] (i.e., balances_after >= balances_before); the mutant that subtracts msg.value from balances breaks this by making balances decrease for some inputs.

For any actor and any deposited amount, calling Deposit increases the total sum of all per-address balances recorded in balances[] by exactly the deposited amount; the mutant that subtracts msg.value from balances can decrease that total for some inputs.

For any depositor address and nonzero ether amount they send via Deposit, the reference contract's balances for that depositor after the call is equal to its previous value plus the sent amount; the mutant that subtracts msg.value will violate this for some inputs (making the depositor's recorded balance decrease).

For any caller and amount, invoking Deposit never decreases any account's recorded balances entry (every balances[key]_after >= balances[key]_before); the mutant that subtracts msg.value can make some account's balance strictly decrease for some inputs.

For every caller and amount, calling Deposit(msg.value) on the correct contract increases that caller's balances mapping by exactly msg.value (so balances(caller) after Deposit == balances(caller) before + msg.value); the mutant that omits the balances update breaks this rule for some inputs because Deposit no longer changes balances.

For any caller and any positive deposit amount, after calling Deposit the reference contract's balances for the caller is increased by the deposited amount; the mutant that omits the balance update will violate this for some caller/amount (i.e., balances(caller) after Deposit == balances(caller) before + msg.value).

For any depositor address and deposit amount, there exists some address key k (specifically the depositor) whose balances increases by the deposited amount after calling Deposit; the mutant that removes the balance update will violate this because balances(k) will not increase for that depositor.

For any addresses a (depositor) and k (arbitrary key) and any value v, if k currently has zero balance and the depositor calls Deposit sending v > 0, then in the reference contract balances(k) remains zero unless k==a (i.e., only the depositor's own balance may change); the mutant that omits updating balances for the depositor can cause balances(a) to remain zero after a positive Deposit while Log still records the deposit, violating this invariant.

For every depositor address and deposit value, the total sum of all balances in the contract increases by exactly the deposited amount after Deposit; the mutant that omits updating balances leaves the total sum unchanged for some deposit, breaking this property.

Reference contract always records in its public log (History) a message whose Val equals the deposited amount after Deposit(...) completes; the mutant that logs zero breaks this because it records Val == 0 for some deposit amounts.

For every Deposit() call the reference contract records in its public History array a Message whose Val equals the deposited amount for the depositor’s final logged entry; the mutant logs 0 instead and thus for some deposit amounts the last History entry's Val will not equal the deposited amount.

For any depositor and deposit amount > 0, after calling Deposit the contract's balances mapping for that depositor equals the sum of prior balance plus the deposited amount (the mutant still increases balances but may cause logged Val mismatches that can lead to different behavior when a callee's fallback fails during Collect; specifically, if a depositor later calls Collect and the low-level call to send Ether fails, balances should remain unchanged in the reference but the mutant's altered logs can change whether Collect proceeds under certain MinSum checks — we assert that immediately after Deposit the depositor's public balances getter increased by exactly the deposited amount).

For any depositor and deposit amount > 0, after calling Deposit through an address whose fallback reverts on plain transfers, the reference C ensures that if the depositor's balance is >= MinSum then a subsequent Collect of <= balance will revert when the recipient's low-level call fails (so balances remain unchanged); the mutant that logs 0 can change observable behavior via Log.AddMessage side-effects in Collect, causing Collect to succeed or balances to change for some inputs — we assert that after Deposit the reference always leaves balances consistent and Collect reverts when the recipient call fails, which the mutant can break.

For any depositor and deposit amount > 0, after calling Deposit the reference contract always logs a History entry whose Val equals the deposited amount for that depositor's latest message index; the mutant that replaces the logged value with 0 will produce a different LastMsg.Val (0) for some deposits, so the rule (Last logged Val equals deposited amount) is violated by the mutant.

Invariant: After any successful Deposit by any caller X, the contract's balances(X) is increased by exactly the sent msg.value in the reference (i.e. balances(X) == old + amt); the mutant that logs before updating can be broken by a malicious Log contract that re-enters during AddMessage so that balances recorded for some address differ (the reference updates balance before the external call so it remains correct).

Reference: Deposit always increments balances(msg.sender) even if Log.AddMessage re-enters or fails — i.e., after Deposit returns successfully, balances(caller) == prior + value; Mutant: because it calls Log.AddMessage before updating balances, a malicious Log that re-enters during AddMessage can cause the final balances mapping to differ (the mutant can be made to leave balances smaller), so the property is violated for some inputs when Log is adversarial.

For any caller and amount, after a successful Deposit call the reference contract C always has balances(caller) >= balances_before(caller) + amount (the caller's balance is increased and cannot be decreased by external reentrancy during logging); the mutant that calls the external Log before updating balances can be re-entered by a malicious Log and leave balances(caller) less than prior+amount for some inputs, so the property is violated.

After any successful Deposit by a caller, the reference C always increments balances(msg.sender) by the deposited amount regardless of Log behavior; the mutant that logs before updating can be re-entered by a malicious Log and can cause balances(msg.sender) to end up less than prior+amount for some inputs.

For any caller and deposit amount, after a successful Deposit the reference C's total recorded sum of all balances (sum over balances for all addresses that interacted via Deposit) increases exactly by the deposited value, whereas the mutant that calls Log.AddMessage before updating balances can be re-entered by a malicious Log contract to manipulate balances of other addresses so the global sum does not increase by the deposited value for some inputs.

For every uint _val the reference contract C allows SetMinSum(_val) to succeed (when not initialized) and sets MinSum to that exact _val; the mutant rejects _val == 0 (reverts) and thus does not set MinSum to 0, breaking the universal property.

For any caller and value, if SetMinSum completes successfully on the reference contract then MinSum equals the provided value; the mutant can revert after assigning MinSum causing MinSum to be updated even though the call reverts (observable difference).
For any caller and value, if SetMinSum reverts then the contract's MinSum must remain unchanged; the mutant assigns MinSum before checking initialization so a reverting call can still change MinSum.

For any caller and any uint value, calling SetMinSum either (A) completes successfully and MinSum equals the provided value, or (B) reverts and leaves MinSum unchanged; the mutant that writes MinSum before the revert can change MinSum even when the call reverts, violating the second case.

For every call to SetMinSum(x), if the call reverts then C.MinSum remains equal to its previous value; the mutant that assigns MinSum before checking initialization can change MinSum even when the call reverts, violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any uint x, calling SetMinSum(x) when the contract is already initialized MUST revert and must NOT change MinSum (reference preserves this; the mutant assigns MinSum before reverting and thus can change MinSum even though the call reverts).

For any nonzero input _val, a fresh (not-yet-initialized) contract C's MinSum after calling SetMinSum(_val) equals exactly _val (reference); the mutant that adds to existing MinSum can produce a different result for some fuzzed _val (e.g., when SetMinSum called twice the value differs).

For any caller and any log address, calling SetLogFile on the correct contract will always set the public Log to the provided address (overwriting any previous value) before initialization; the mutant prevents overwriting when Log is already non-zero, so for some inputs the stored Log differs after the call.

For any caller and any _log address, calling SetLogFile on the correct contract always results in c.Log() equaling the passed address (it overwrites any prior non-zero Log before initialization); the mutant prevents overwriting when Log is already set, so after a second SetLogFile call the stored Log can differ from the passed address.

For any two addresses a and b (possibly equal), after calling SetLogFile(a) then SetLogFile(b) on the correct contract, the public Log getter returns b (the second argument) — the mutant prevents overwriting an already-set Log, so for some a,b the final Log differs.

For any two addresses a and b, if SetLogFile(a) then SetLogFile(b) are called before initialization, the reference contract's public Log getter equals b (the second set overwrites), while the mutant sometimes keeps the first value and so the final Log != b.

For any two non-zero addresses a and b, if SetLogFile(a) then SetLogFile(b) are both called before Initialized(), the reference implementation always sets the public Log to b (the second address) while the mutant may keep the first address when b is different from a.

For any non-zero address passed to SetLogFile before initialization, the correct contract sets the public Log getter to that address (Log != address(0)), while the mutant unconditionally clears it to address(0) and thus violates this for some inputs.

For any non-zero address passed to SetLogFile before initialization, the reference contract's public Log getter returns that address (Log == supplied address), whereas the mutant sets Log to address(0) and thus will differ for some non-zero inputs.

For any non-zero address provided to SetLogFile before initialization, the reference contract records that address in its public Log getter, whereas the mutant clears Log to address(0) and thus will make the public Log getter equal address(0) for some inputs.

For any non-zero address passed to SetLogFile before initialization, the reference contract stores that address in its public Log getter (address(c.Log()) == supplied), whereas the mutant clears Log to address(0) and thus violates that rule for some non-zero inputs.

For any non-zero address _log passed to SetLogFile before initialization, the reference stores that address in its public Log getter (address(c.Log()) == _log); the mutant instead clears Log to address(0) and thus violates this for some non-zero _log inputs.

For any caller and any address argument, calling SetLogFile(x) on the correct contract always updates the public Log state to x (when not initialized), whereas the mutant leaves Log unchanged for all non-zero callers—so there exist inputs (non-zero caller) where the mutant fails to set Log but the reference sets it.

For any caller and any address argument when C is not initialized, calling SetLogFile(address) sets the public Log to that address; the mutant only sets Log when msg.sender==address(0) and thus fails to set Log for normal callers (some inputs).

For any caller and log-address input when C is not initialized, calling SetLogFile(_log) results in the public Log getter returning _log; the mutant only assigns Log when msg.sender==address(0) and thus for many (non-zero) callers the public Log differs after the call.

For any caller A and any address L when C is not initialized, calling SetLogFile(L) causes the public Log getter to return L; the mutant only assigns Log when msg.sender==address(0) and thus for typical nonzero callers the getter does not equal L.

For any caller address A and any log-address L when C is not yet initialized, calling SetLogFile(L) results in the public Log getter returning L; the mutant only assigns Log when msg.sender==address(0) and therefore for typical nonzero callers the getter does not equal L (so there exist inputs where the mutant breaks this rule).

For any address provided, calling SetLogFile on the correct contract succeeds (does not revert) and sets the Log file pointer (public getter changes from zero to that address); the mutant always reverts so this property is violated for inputs where the caller is allowed to call SetLogFile (i.e. before Initialized).

For any address target and any caller before initialization, calling SetLogFile(target) on the correct contract returns (does not revert) and sets the Log pointer to target; the mutant unconditionally reverts causing the call to fail and Log not to be set for some inputs.

For any caller and any target address passed before initialization, the reference C successfully accepts SetLogFile(target) (call returns) and sets the public Log getter to that target; the mutant always reverts from SetLogFile so for some fuzzed target/caller the call fails and Log remains unchanged.
